newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP sees 10-yr life for NZ Steel operation.
newsitem.headline: BHP sees 10-yr life for NZ Steel operation.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), unveiling its long term steel strategy, said on Tuesday it could not envisage any replacement of New Zealand Steel's facilities when they required replacement in about 10 years.

"While we have significantly enhanced the plant's potential by doubling productivity in the last five years and investing in new metal coating facilities, it is difficult to envisage the replacement of the plant's steelmaking facilities at the end of their current life, estimated to be no more than 10 years," BHP Steel chief executive Ron McNeilly said.
"Indeed, should business conditions not improve, it is entirely possible that the steelmaking facilities will close earlier," McNeilly said.

He said the New Zealand operations were sub-scale and the business was under increasing pressure from weakening domestic market demand, depressed international steel prices and a strong New Zealand dollar.

"In addition, New Zealand Steel's steelmaking facilities are based on a relatively complex technology." The New Zealand operation produces about 700,000 tonnes a year and has about 1,600 employees. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
